Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of that same problem. Each call does a small piece of work and then hands the rest off to another call of itself, until it reaches a simple case it can answer directly (called the base case). That final answer then bubbles back up through all the waiting calls, like a stack of plates being unwound. The two things to get right are always having a base case so it doesn't loop forever, and making sure each recursive call moves closer to that base case.
